notes.title: Major Update: Dust Raiders v1.1.1
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/50e15e75fb8debba2cb28084a2dab698435f03b3.png"]
Major Update: Dust Raiders v1.1.1
The desert roads will never be the same. Our latest major update brings a host of new features, balance changes, and fixes that expand your journey through the world of Dust Raiders.
New Features
Free Play after Story Completion - Finishing the main storyline is just the beginning. Continue your adventure freely without restrictions!

Crew Bonuses from Cargo - Some crew members now provide benefits even when stationed in Cargo. Move them into vehicles for additional bonuses.

Workshop Randomization - Workshop inventories now refresh daily, and items you sell will appear in stock.

New Equipment Tier - A new tier of gear has been introduced, expanding upgrade paths and build variety.

Looted Module Upgrade Chance - Combat loot now has a small chance to appear at a higher tier.
Balance Adjustments
Adjusted the range of the Twin Launcher.

Rebalanced prices of certain crew members and modules.
Fixes
Unused vehicles in the Caravan panel are no longer incorrectly marked as destroyed.



This is the biggest update to Dust Raiders since launch, and it is only the beginning of what we have planned. Keep your eyes open! Update #2 – with New Game Modes is on the way!!!

Thank you for your support and constant feedback.

See you on the desert trails.

notes.title: Dust Raiders v1.0.6 Update – Enemy Stun Reduction
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/50e15e75fb8debba2cb28084a2dab698435f03b3.png"]

Hello Raiders!

We’ve heard your feedback loud and clear - many of you mentioned that the amount of stun effects from enemies, especially in the later stages of the game, felt overwhelming and disrupted the gameplay experience.

In response, the latest update 1.0.6 reduces the number of enemies equipped with the Oil Spiller ability, which was a major source of stuns.  In previous updates, we also shortened the duration of stuns - which should also have a positive impact on gameplay balance.

This change aims to make combat smoother and more enjoyable without compromising the challenge.

We truly appreciate your ongoing support and detailed feedback. Keep it coming, and stay tuned for more improvements!

Hey Raiders!

We’ve just released version 1.0.5, bringing a mix of quality-of-life improvements, UI tweaks, and a few important fixes based on your feedback. Check out what's new:

notes.title: 🛠 Dust Raiders v1.0.4 – Update & Vehicle System Rework
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/203abc64a6a0760f4aab920550418a22786d4fbb.png"]



🛠 Dust Raiders v1.0.4 – Update & Vehicle System Rework

Hey Raiders!
Update v1.0.4 is here, bringing a major overhaul to how destroyed vehicles work, along with some gameplay improvements and important bug fixes. Here’s what’s new:
[hr][/hr]🚗 Reworked Destroyed Vehicle Mechanics:
Destroyed vehicles are no longer permanently lost – they now remain in your caravan as broken.

However, there's still a chance you’ll lose some equipment from them.

Broken vehicles cannot participate in encounters and don’t increase your cargo limit.

You can repair them at Service Stations or sell them at Workshops.

Any lost cargo is now stored in the caravan wreckage, so it can still be recovered.
[hr][/hr]⚙️ Gameplay Improvements:
Goods transferred from factories now go directly to your Cargo, instead of the enclave Warehouse.

There is now a chance to earn fuel as a reward for winning encounters – every drop counts in the wasteland!
[hr][/hr]🐞 Bug Fixes:
Fixed an issue where fog of war progress was lost after changing scenes without saving.

Fixed several bugs that could cause combat to get stuck.
[hr][/hr]
Thanks again for all your feedback and bug reports – your support helps us keep Dust Raiders moving forward!
Stay safe out there... and remember, even a wreck might ride again. 🚛💥

– The Dust Raiders Team

notes.title: Dust Raiders v1.0.3 Update
notes.content:
Dust Raiders v1.0.3 – Changelog


🔧 Listening to your feedback, we’re introducing some gameplay changes:

Jobs became the most profitable source of income in the previous version. That was never the intended design. Trading goods should be the main income, while Jobs are meant to be a supplement or a fallback option when you lose everything. With this patch, we’re restoring the balance from the Demo and Beta versions: Trading yields higher profits, fewer job offers, and lower rewards.

When you lose a crew member due to an event, the game now removes the least valuable crew member from Cargo first. If there is no crew in Cargo, the least valuable crew member from your vehicles is removed instead.

The chance of losing gear and crew from destroyed vehicles has been reduced from 30% to 20%. Still, if the entire caravan is destroyed, preserved items are stored in the wreck at the crash site. If only an escort vehicle is lost, the preserved items will be assigned to your Cargo.

Wanderer mode autosave now triggers only at safe points — when entering or leaving an enclave, or quitting the game. This ensures that if you haven’t created a manual save, you can still return to a relatively safe moment. Manual saving is still available at any time.

🔧 Other Fixes and Changes:

Added a Garage site to the Windmill enclave

Increased Hell Laser rotation speed for better tracking of fast targets

Fixed issue with invincible vehicles during combat

Fixed the issue with vehicles not being destroyed by large obstacles

Improved some localization issues

Adjusted volume for some sound effects

We hope these changes bring a little more joy to your gameplay :)

notes.title: Dust Raiders Demo v0.7.9 is Live
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/cb03187b644d5d56656013b56929ad0b21d8abe4.png

We're excited to release Dust Raiders Demo v0.7.9, a significant update our small team has been diligently working on for the past two weeks. We've carefully reviewed and incorporated your valuable feedback, aiming to address as many reported issues and suggestions as possible. Please keep in mind that we're a very small team, and while we strive to improve the game consistently, your patience and understanding are greatly appreciated.

Check out the full changelog below, and as always, thank you for your ongoing support!

Dust Raiders v0.7.9 Changelog

Gameplay & Balancing

Additional random Points of Interest now appear on the map.
Jobs in enclaves no longer point to locations inaccessible to the player.
Combat slow-motion now nearly stops time, is no longer time-limited, and can be toggled freely without holding down the space bar.
The next wave of enemies in combat appears immediately after defeating all current enemies.
Increased Recon Scanner range.
Jobs-related cargo is no longer lost when the caravan is destroyed.
The Alcohol delivery to the Plenty enclave mechanism was reworked to give the player better control. We also reduced the amount of alcohol required for delivery.
Early-game combat encounters have become easier.
Player escort vehicles now have increased Durability.
Sniper-equipped enemies now attack the closest vehicle, making it easier to avoid player vehicle destruction.
Pushing enemies into obstacles has become easier.
Increased fuel tank capacity, compensated by adjusted fuel consumption and reduced refueling costs for better realism.
Increased equipment selling price in the Workshop from 25% to 35% of the purchase price.
Reduced the cost of bribing attacking gangs.

UI & UX Improvements

Added the ability to preview active vehicle stats in the garage.
Added cargo and warehouse icons to give a clearer indication of their purpose.
Added a hint on how to skip the intro.
Courier Job cargo is now clearly displayed on Job Boards.
Item icons are now centered on the cursor during drag-and-drop for easier placement.
Newly purchased vehicles automatically join your caravan (if a free slot is available).
Now you can leave locations and enclaves using the ESC key.
A bug-reporting button was added to the combat interface.
Improved the description of damage dealt by the Shotgun.
Valuable rumors can now be purchased at the Shelter enclave (previously free so often ignored 😄).
Improved enemy targeting in tutorial combat.

Bug Fixes

Fixed animations for heavy vehicle damage.
Fixed Oil Spiller functionality.
Fixed issues causing the Rocket Launcher to deal no damage occasionally.
Fixed Ramming action animations.
Cargo Hold Extension modules tier 2 and 3 now function correctly.
Resolved issues with selecting higher resolutions on some monitors.
Fixed issues related to the Side Slam action.
Fixed bugs occurring when rapidly spamming combat actions.
Crew member fuel cost reduction effect now functions correctly.
Burning debris sound near the Refinery now only plays when debris is visible.
The first game event now displays the correct name.
Numerous translation errors have been fixed.


Enjoy your adventure in the wastelands!

notes.title: HOTFIX for Dust Raiders Demo – Bug Fixes & Improvements!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/3dc3a9ffb31040ec15f6682e71c85e6e06dff01c.pngDust Raiders v0.7.8 Changelog

Gameplay & Mechanics

Fuel Consumption Reduced: Fuel consumption is now cut in half, allowing for extended exploration without refueling.

Bug Fixes

 Intro playback: Fixed an issue where the intro video would fail to play on some systems, causing the game to hang.
 Tutorial stuck condition: Fixed a bug where a special action during the “targeting enemy” tutorial step could cause the combat to become stuck.
 Auto-targeting in first combat: Addressed problems when tutorial hints were disabled, ensuring proper enemy targeting behavior.
 Missing “Out of Fuel” tutorial hint: Players will now receive the intended hint when running out of fuel.
 Enemy Durability: Potential fix of an issue where enemies occasionally remained alive at zero durability.
 Exploration Music Loop: Fixed looping errors that caused background music to repeat inappropriately.

UI & Visuals

 Cargo & Warehouse Icons: Added clearer icons to help players distinguish these storage features at a glance.

We sincerely appreciate your dedication and involvement in helping us improve Dust Raiders. Your detailed feedback, bug reports, and suggestions have been incredibly valuable, and we’re grateful for your active participation in shaping the game. Thank you for being such an engaged and supportive community!

notes.title: Dust Raiders - A UI Designed for Survival - Devlog #05
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/73ce92f32f58c0becc4d4a24a35e70cba5b60c18.png

In the harsh world of Dust Raiders, information is power, and a well-designed user interface (UI) can mean the difference between life and death. Today, we're excited to give you a sneak peek into the UI of Dust Raiders and how it enhances your gameplay experience.

Concept vs the current design
The first version of the UI was created for the trailer when the game was in early development. As the project progressed, our needs evolved. However, this initial design helped establish the general mood, and the final icon design is a natural evolution of that style.

We've refined the icons, but more importantly, we've added clearer and more contextual information around your Caravan.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/1463e9ea37e3f0a64a7ba28d8da47f34796e9f72.png

In the heat of battle, every second counts. That's why we've designed our combat UI to be both informative and unobtrusive. It provides all the crucial information - health, ammunition, enemy positions - without cluttering your screen. The result is a fluid combat experience that lets you focus on the action while making tactical decisions on the fly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/fe12b53c449862d93eec12b4cd04c1d7c23c4bb8.png

The vehicle part now takes slightly more space to make sure you can see the attack icons, status, health and shield. We have also added red elements on the raider’s armor to make sure to more clearly distinguish them between enemies and foes.

Enclaves - the last prospering settlements
Before driving into the unforgiving desert, you must carefully plan your route. This involves locating optimal enclaves to ensure you can meet demand with goods from nearby settlements.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/5ae39743287d2b9c3f80304cb3c59e14f46989f4.png

Each enclave features unique artwork to help you identify its location. The same applies to Points of Interest (POIs) scattered across the map. Just keep in mind that the array of buildings and available services differs between enclaves.

Wasteland Trader
In the world of Dust Raiders, resources are scarce, and trading is crucial for survival. Our focus is to make sure the dynamic supply and demand, resource availability, pricing and your cargo capacity are all quickly glanceable and adjustable at the one view.

On the left side you can see the current stock meter which is the key indicator regarding the needs of the enclave. It takes time to restock and information on the right will help you identify the source of resources and the dedicated supply chains.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/ca0ab8728be37120f7055378470e5df69d79a447.png

Ruthless fleet
Last but not least is the vehicle and weapon crew management. This crucial element ensures you're prepared for any encounters. You'll need to strategically assign your crew to maximize your chances of survival in the unforgiving wasteland.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/7c31175a012ac9ef83385f40f75fc4ed8fa187cd.png

Your caravan consists of the main vehicle, which has the most customizable slots, including special weapons and up to 2 crew members. The supporting cars have less slots and much more fragile. You can also see your maximum cargo capacity or a set of unused vehicles if you have managed to secure more for your fleet.

And that’s it for today’s devlog!
In the coming updates, we will delve deeper into the other gameplay elements of Dust Raiders. So, keep your engines running, and stay tuned for more exciting news about your favorite post-apocalyptic vehicular combat game. Remember, in Dust Raiders, it's not just about surviving - it's about thriving.
We'll see you in the wastelands.

notes.title: Dust Raiders - The World - Devlog #01/2024
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/35cb13d34a57035a910f4293b923d81bce2c478a.png

From the borders of the Eternal Desert to contaminated marshes and abandoned Polis, the world of Dust Raiders is for the toughest. And even those considered reckless will only survive with proper armor thickness and well-oiled machinery. 

In this devlog, we will start a monthly series sharing our inspirations, gameplay features, and development updates for Dust Raiders. Buckle up, and let's start the engines!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/806f491c2295ce179a0d6b43eaf7b4a944af6719.png

The world has shrunk
It's been a long time since humanity broke the Earth's balance. The climate changed so vastly we can't even pinpoint the exact location. The old countries' names and continents are no longer used, with new practical ones being used.

The world shrinks immensely for the majority of people who remain alive. Worrying about their safety, they settled in small enclaves, desperately looking for resources and jobs that helped them make a living. But none of them could survive independently - mines are only located next to some of them, some have a better climate to grow plants, etc. They need to trade.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/582b8de53138af3fc90a4f0f0b6b688b99fb3d85.png


The desolate spread between them is harsh, overrun by raiders, gangs and self-acclaimed rulers waiting for goods to be taken by force. Achieving a good balance between safety and profit differentiates random traders from the most influential ones. And it will be your journey to ride along.

Recycling is all that's left
People establishing enclaves need to work with whatever materials are at their disposal. Sheet metal is relatively cheap and easily adjustable, although it's not the best when the sun hits hard. Fortunately, clouds do appear in this world. 

Humanity took a considerable step back in technology. Fortunately, the knowledge of extracting oil was not lost, and the power of petrol and diesel engines helped to fight the dark and cold nights.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/47a2578e051d5b5e2fc5e226b925b27a44cc89da.png

Post-apocalyptic visions of small American villages inspire the design of the enclaves. The people there use whatever materials they can find to build their homes and defences, such as sheet metal, wood, concrete, and scrap. They also rely on oil and diesel engines to power their machines and vehicles, as they need to gain knowledge of more advanced technologies.

You might ask, why didn't people move on from such a harsh location to live in? Well, apart from the oil availability, they also can't. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/df6d42642e790cde761703bf5e76f591726ced3c.png

It is surrounded by Eternal Dunes from one side, contaminated water from the other and huge mountains with collapsed tunnels. Stuck, trying to find a habitable place across the desert, nearby marshes and dunes. But also a perfect trade opportunity to rule the local economy in this new reality.

Stay tuned for more!
Our ride will take some time, and we will dive deep into various gameplay elements, our development process, or more stuff coming to Dust Raiders. Remember to add Dust Raiders to your wishlist and follow us on Steam.

See you next month!
